purpose: Source universe for the weekly St Georges Strategy Intelligence and AI Signals refresh.

sourceTiers.primary: Official regulator, central bank, standard-setter, company, academic, or government source.
sourceTiers.specialist: Recognised trade, legal, cyber, technology, market, or financial-services publication.
sourceTiers.press: General media used for market colour, company news, or early reports where primary sources are not yet available.

sources.name: Financial Conduct Authority
signalQuestions: Has the FCA changed expectations for firms, boards, senior managers, or customer outcomes?
Is there a consultation, speech, enforcement action, or deadline that needs an owner?

sources.name: Financial Services Regulatory Initiatives Grid
signalQuestions: Has a planned regulatory initiative, milestone, consultation, or implementation window changed?
Does a horizon item need a named owner before the next board or committee cycle?

sources.name: Financial Conduct Authority Enforcement Notices
signalQuestions: Does an FCA notice reveal a repeatable conduct, governance, financial-crime, or control failure pattern?
Does the notice create a control-owner question or deadline for remediation evidence?

sources.name: Bank of England and Prudential Regulation Authority
signalQuestions: Has prudential, resilience, or financial-stability language shifted?
Are banks, insurers, FMIs, stablecoins, or nonbanks being pulled into a new control expectation?

sources.name: European Central Bank Banking Supervision
signalQuestions: Does the ECB point to a supervisory priority, thematic review, or governance weakness?
Does the signal translate into a control-owner challenge for UK or global firms?

sources.name: ECB Banking Supervision Newsletter
signalQuestions: Does the SSM newsletter reveal a supervisory priority, implementation theme, or recurring weakness?
Does the item translate into a board, risk committee, or control-owner question?

sources.name: ECB Banking Supervision Priorities and Risks
signalQuestions: Have ECB supervisory priorities, risk themes, or expectations shifted?
Does a priority create a horizon item or control challenge for banks and global groups?

sources.name: European Banking Authority
signalQuestions: Has the EBA published final guidance, consultation, technical standards, or risk analysis?
Does it create a near-term implementation date or policy dependency?

sources.name: European Securities and Markets Authority
signalQuestions: Is there a market-structure, investor-protection, reporting, or crypto signal?
Does the item affect trading, asset management, wealth, or surveillance teams?

sources.name: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
signalQuestions: Has EIOPA changed expectations for insurers, occupational pensions, conduct, resilience, or supervisory reporting?
Does the item create an implementation date, board question, or control-owner action for insurance or pension businesses?

sources.name: Bank for International Settlements
signalQuestions: Is a macro-financial vulnerability becoming relevant to financial-institution risk appetite?
Does the signal point to concentration, leverage, liquidity, valuation, or infrastructure fragility?

sources.name: Financial Stability Board
signalQuestions: Is the FSB signalling global convergence or divergence in financial-stability expectations?
Does the item create a topic for boards, risk committees, or cross-border policy teams?

sources.name: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
signalQuestions: Has the Basel Committee changed standards, monitoring, implementation expectations, or disclosure requirements?
Does the item affect capital planning, risk-weighted assets, liquidity, or supervisory reporting?

sources.name: IOSCO
signalQuestions: Is IOSCO signalling global market-conduct expectations?
Does the item affect funds, market infrastructure, trading venues, or investor protection?

sources.name: US Securities and Exchange Commission
signalQuestions: Is there a US market, disclosure, enforcement, or crypto signal with global read-across?
Does it affect listed issuers, asset managers, brokers, exchanges, or advisers?

sources.name: US Commodity Futures Trading Commission
signalQuestions: Is there a derivatives, clearing, crypto, or commodity-market signal?
Does it affect market conduct, surveillance, client risk, or margin assumptions?

sources.name: UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation
signalQuestions: Has sanctions guidance, enforcement, licensing, or reporting changed?
Does the item create a control update for screening, payments, onboarding, or escalation?

sources.name: Financial Action Task Force
signalQuestions: Has FATF changed financial-crime, AML, CTF, sanctions, or crypto expectations?
Does the item create a cross-border control question for onboarding, monitoring, screening, or escalation?

sources.name: FinCEN Enforcement Actions
signalQuestions: Does a FinCEN action reveal a repeatable AML, reporting, monitoring, or governance failure pattern?
Does the enforcement release create a practical control-owner question for financial-crime teams?

sources.name: OFAC Recent Actions
signalQuestions: Has OFAC issued a sanctions action, guidance, penalty, or update that changes screening or escalation priorities?
Does the item indicate a control weakness firms should test across payments, onboarding, or transaction monitoring?

sources.name: AMF Enforcement Committee News Releases
signalQuestions: Does an AMF sanction reveal a market-conduct, disclosure, governance, or control failure pattern?
Does the release create a board, compliance, or control-owner question for firms with EU market activity?

sources.name: ECB Banking Supervision Sanctions
signalQuestions: Has the ECB imposed or updated a sanction that reveals a prudential, governance, reporting, or control weakness?
Does the sanction create an implementation lesson for supervised banks or global banking groups?

sources.name: UK National Cyber Security Centre
signalQuestions: Is there a threat, advisory, or resilience lesson relevant to financial services?
Does it affect critical services, suppliers, identity, cloud, payments, or incident response?

sources.name: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
signalQuestions: Is there an exploited vulnerability or advisory that should trigger control-owner action?
Does the advisory touch widely used software, cloud services, identity, or managed service providers?

sources.name: OpenAI
signalQuestions: Has OpenAI changed model capability, product packaging, enterprise controls, or safety positioning?
Does the item change adoption, vendor-risk, or governance assumptions for regulated firms?

sources.name: Anthropic
signalQuestions: Has Anthropic changed model capability, access controls, enterprise controls, or safety posture?
Does the signal affect model-risk, cyber-risk, procurement, or agent deployment?

sources.name: Google DeepMind
signalQuestions: Has Google changed the frontier model, multimodal, robotics, or research landscape?
Does the item create a governance issue for physical-world AI, enterprise use, or vendor concentration?

sources.name: Meta AI
signalQuestions: Has Meta changed open-model capability, release posture, tooling, safety, or distribution?
Does the item alter enterprise adoption, open-source dependency, or model-governance assumptions?

sources.name: Mistral AI
signalQuestions: Has Mistral changed model capability, product packaging, enterprise controls, or European AI positioning?
Does the item change procurement, sovereignty, governance, or vendor-concentration assumptions?

sources.name: xAI
signalQuestions: Has xAI changed model capability, release posture, infrastructure, or distribution?
Does the item create a market, safety, governance, or platform-dependency signal?

sources.name: Microsoft AI
signalQuestions: Has Microsoft changed enterprise AI distribution, Copilot controls, developer tooling, or cloud dependency?
Does the item affect regulated-firm adoption, data controls, or operational resilience?

sources.name: NVIDIA Newsroom
signalQuestions: Has chip, data-centre, sovereign AI, or infrastructure dependency changed?
Does the item affect capital concentration, supplier risk, energy assumptions, or vendor lock-in?

sources.name: arXiv AI and machine learning research
signalQuestions: Is there credible research that changes the interpretation of model capability, risk, or adoption?
Is the paper strong enough to cite, or should it remain a monitoring signal?

sources.name: European Commission EU AI Act
signalQuestions: Has the European Commission changed EU AI Act implementation guidance, timelines, or supervisory expectations?
Does the item create a compliance, model-risk, procurement, or board question for regulated firms using AI?

sources.name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act Tracker
signalQuestions: Does the tracker clarify an EU AI Act implementation milestone that should be checked against primary Commission material?
Does the item help translate official AI Act obligations into a board or control-owner planning question?

sources.name: Epoch AI
signalQuestions: Does Epoch AI provide capability, compute, or economic evidence that changes the interpretation of model progress?
Is the data current enough to cite, or should the item be flagged as older than 90 days?

sources.name: LMArena
signalQuestions: Has a leaderboard movement changed practical model-selection or capability assumptions?
Does the result need corroboration with model cards, system cards, or primary release notes before publication?

sources.name: Stanford HAI AI Index
signalQuestions: Does the AI Index provide the right annual anchor statistic for AI adoption, capability, investment, or governance?
Is the statistic older than 90 days and therefore something to flag rather than present as current movement?

sources.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
signalQuestions: Has NIST changed AI RMF guidance, profiles, playbooks, or implementation material?
Does the update create a governance control, assurance, or board question that cross-feeds the Virtual Officer brief?

sources.name: Import AI
signalQuestions: Does Import AI surface a research, policy, model, or industry signal missed by daily source sweeps?
Can the signal be traced back to a primary lab, paper, regulator, or company source before publication?

sources.name: The Batch
signalQuestions: Does The Batch catch a practical AI signal that should be checked against a primary source?
Does the item help prioritise model, product, governance, or industry cards for AI Signals?

sources.name: Financial Times
signalQuestions: Is the item useful market colour, company intelligence, or early read-through?
Can the main claim be corroborated with a primary or second specialist source?

sources.name: Reuters Regulatory News
signalQuestions: Does Reuters corroborate a regulatory, enforcement, incident, or market-structure claim from a primary source?
Is there a primary regulator, company, court, or official document that should be cited instead as the lead source?

sources.name: ORX News and Blogs
signalQuestions: Does ORX identify an operational-risk event or pattern that should be checked against primary incident sources?
Does the item help distinguish a one-off event from a repeatable control failure theme?

sources.name: Global Regulation Tomorrow
signalQuestions: Does Regulation Tomorrow clarify what a regulatory deadline, consultation, or supervisory update means in practice?
Can the interpretation be traced back to the regulator or primary legal text before publication?

sources.name: Sidley Insights
signalQuestions: Does Sidley provide useful interpretation of a financial-services regulatory change or deadline?
Is the interpretation backed by a primary regulator, statute, consultation, or enforcement source?

sources.name: A&O Shearman Insights
signalQuestions: Does A&O Shearman add practical interpretation of a regulatory, DORA, markets, or governance deadline?
Can the item be checked against primary legal text, regulator publications, or official consultations before citation?

sources.name: Risk.net
signalQuestions: Does the item reveal how practitioners are interpreting a rule, model, or market-risk issue?
Is it an implementation detail that official sources do not cover?

sources.name: Finextra
signalQuestions: Is there a payment, fintech, bank-technology, or digital-asset signal with operational impact?
Does it need corroboration from a firm, regulator, or scheme owner?

sources.name: The Register
signalQuestions: Is there a technology outage, vulnerability, cloud dependency, or infrastructure issue relevant to resilience?
Can the item be linked to a vendor advisory or official incident page?

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
signalQuestions: Is there an AI company, funding, product, or market signal that needs a primary source check?
Does the item create a useful industry card after corroboration with company or official material?

sources.name: The Verge AI
signalQuestions: Is there a platform, consumer-AI, policy, or product signal that needs a primary source check?
Does the item help explain industry consequence without becoming the lead citation for official claims?

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
signalQuestions: Is there a technical AI development, research dispute, or platform signal with governance implications?
Can the item be corroborated with model release notes, research papers, or official product material?

sources.name: Reuters
signalQuestions: Is this a timely company, market, or regulatory development not yet available in a primary source?
Can it be corroborated before publication?
